confirmed: Source identity verified: arXiv:2608.12605v1 [cs.HC], 12 Aug 2026, with DOI 10.1145/3830398.3830612 on the first page; the title and all seven authors match the form. The PDF has 19 pages. The entire markdown conversion was read through Appendix B, with numerical claims checked in PDF text (p. 1; pp. 12-19, Appendices A-B).

No randomized people study is documented. The evaluation states that condition order was counterbalanced, and the limitations describe seven participants in each order group without saying that order was randomized. The formative study has no assigned AI comparison. has_randomized_people_study=false means no reported qualifying randomization was found, not proof that an unreported procedure was nonrandom (p. 4, Section 3; p. 8, Section 6; p. 11, Section 8).

The retained design_class=other and context_class=none are consistent with a counterbalanced tool-evaluation study whose randomization is not stated: the paper is neither an AI-versus-human output comparison nor a synthesis, and it does not report an observational across-person creativity/diversity comparison. Do not recode it as an RCT from counterbalancing alone (p. 8, Section 6; pp. 9 and 15, LPIPS description and results).

The evaluation has 14 people analyzed, the same participants in both conditions; the two arm counts of 14 must not be added together. Table 1 lists P1-P14, and final-design galleries likewise identify P1-P14. Randomized counts remain null, and no exclusions are reported. The form correctly records fewer than 50 people and core=no (p. 8, Section 6; p. 15, Table 1; pp. 18-19, Figures 15-16).

The participant details match: ages 24-47, eight men and six women, professional design backgrounds, online/community recruitment, and $30 compensation. No participant country is specified; author affiliations should not supply it (p. 8, Section 6).

Both conditions involved poster design with AI; participants used the same topic and the same three to four references, with 20 minutes per condition in an approximately 90-minute session. The baseline removed axis-centered interactions from an otherwise equivalent system (p. 8, Section 6).
The system uses a 3-by-3 grid, Gemini-2.5-Flash-Lite for the vision-language pipeline, and Gemini-2.5-Flash-Image for image generation (p. 5, Section 4.1.1; p. 12, Appendix A.1).

S1-O1 reported values match exactly: Mean LPIPS=0.641>0.529, p=0.0001. Table 1 Overall gives Baseline 0.529 (0.078) and Surprise2Refine 0.641 (0.080), with columns labeled Mean (SD) (p. 9, Section 7.1; p. 15, Table 1).

LPIPS concerns each participant's initial nine generated designs under the same moodboard references and prompts. These are image outputs, not additional participants or final-poster ratings; the metric does not measure homogenization across different people. The precise LPIPS backbone and pair aggregation procedure are not stated (p. 15, Appendix B.1 and Table 1; pp. 16-18, Figures 11-14).

S1-O2 reported values match exactly: Q12 MD=5>3.5; p=0.006. Q12 is the post-tool self-report "This tool helped me to be more creative" on the 7-point questionnaire; the results section names a Wilcoxon signed-rank test (p. 8, Section 7; p. 9, Section 7.1 and Figure 8).

S1-O3 reported values match exactly: CSI=69.71>55.79; p=0.0085. This is a post-condition self-report index, with additional CSI item distributions and scale scores in Appendix B (p. 8, Sections 6 and 7.1; pp. 15-16, Appendix B.2, Figure 10 and Table 2).

Every numerical value in the one_line_finding matches the cited PDF passages; the contrasts should be interpreted as results of the reported counterbalanced comparison, with randomization not stated (pp. 8-9, Section 7.1; p. 15, Table 1).

This is original system-development and user-study research, not a synthesis; no study-count meta-analysis, pooled estimate, interval, or effect standardizer should be entered in synthesis (p. 4, Section 3; p. 8, Section 6; p. 11, Section 9).
summary: The 14-designer comparison reports counterbalancing but no random assignment, and all quoted headline statistics match the PDF. Corrections address the omitted formative study, Adobe involvement, included appendices, unresolved form fields, and unsupported wording about final-poster creativity ratings.
